configMismatch.title: Config path mismatch
configMismatch.body: RouteBox edits {ours}, but the systemd unit {service}.service starts amnezia-box with {unit}. Changes will not reach the running process. Starting and restarting are blocked until this is resolved.
configMismatch.useUnitHint: Adopting moves RouteBox onto the path in {service}.service's ExecStart and leaves the unit alone. Whichever fix you pick, a process that is already running keeps reading the file it was started with until it is restarted.
configMismatch.foreignUnit: The detected unit is {service}.service, not amnezia-box.service. Only "Point {service}.service at our config" changes that unit; adopting the unit's config path changes RouteBox itself and leaves the unit alone. Make sure this is the installation RouteBox should manage.
configMismatch.fixed: The systemd unit now uses the RouteBox config path.
configMismatch.notPersisted: The new path is in use, but could not be written to the settings file: RouteBox will fall back to the old one when it restarts, and this fix will have to be repeated. {error}
configMismatch.refreshFailed: The action went through, but the panel could not re-read the status. Reload the page.
configMismatch.restartTitle: The running process uses a different config file
configMismatch.restartBody: amnezia-box was started with {process} and keeps reading that file, while RouteBox edits {ours}. Only a restart moves it onto {ours} — changing a path does not reach a process that is already running. Active connections will be dropped.
configMismatch.failed: Could not resolve the config path mismatch: {error}

configDropIn.title: RouteBox is holding {service}.service on its config path
configDropIn.body: A RouteBox drop-in at {file} overrides ExecStart so {service}.service starts amnezia-box with {path}. The unit file itself is untouched and its other arguments are kept.
configDropIn.bodyUnknown: A RouteBox drop-in at {file} overrides ExecStart of {service}.service, but its contents could not be read — open the file to see what it sets.
configDropIn.pending: systemd has not picked the file up yet: the unit still starts amnezia-box with {unit}. It will apply at the next daemon-reload or reboot.
configDropIn.removeHint: Removing it deletes the file, runs daemon-reload and puts {service}.service back on its own ExecStart. If that is not {ours}, the config path mismatch comes back and starting, restarting and reloading are blocked again until you resolve it another way.
configDropIn.removed: The drop-in is removed and {service}.service is back on its own ExecStart.
configDropIn.removedPartly: The drop-in file is deleted, but the removal is not fully in effect yet. {error}

server.ccClientDecides: Off: each client decides. A client that announces its own rates gets Brutal, one that announces none gets BBR.

server.ccBrutalOnly: On, with a Down limit: clients that announce no rate of their own are REFUSED — they get an authentication failure and the server logs it at debug level only. Links issued by this panel carry no rates, so this turns away every client you handed out. Only clients configured with their own Up/Down get in, held to the rates above.
server.quicCCHint: Governs the HTTP/3 (QUIC) listener only; TCP connections are unaffected. Default is BBR. The server side offers two algorithms the client side does not.

awg.disableCookiesHint: Stops the server answering the challenge packet it sends under load. One-sided, does not break compatibility.

subscriptions.description: Import and auto-update outbound nodes from a subscription URL. Nodes appear on the Outbounds page with a prefix; manual edits are overwritten on refresh.
subscriptions.name: Name
subscriptions.deleteConfirm: Delete subscription "{name}" and all its nodes?
subscriptions.empty: No subscriptions yet. Add one to import nodes.

auth.insecureWarning: This panel is served over unencrypted HTTP — use HTTPS (reverse proxy) before exposing it publicly.

telegram.title: Telegram proxy
telegram.description: An MTProto proxy for Telegram, run by RouteBox itself. Add clients and share their links.
telegram.loadFailed: Failed to load the Telegram proxy
telegram.emptyDesc: Add one to get a link you can send to someone.
telegram.rotateConfirm: Issue a new secret for “{name}”? Their current link stops working immediately.
telegram.deleteConfirm: Delete “{name}”? Their link stops working immediately.
telegram.linkBlocked: Set a masking domain and a public host before sharing links.
telegram.groupLinksNote: Only needed when a reverse proxy or SNI router sits in front — otherwise leave both empty.
telegram.listenHint: Where the proxy binds. Not the panel's own port.
telegram.maskingDomainHint: The site the proxy impersonates. Anything that fails to authenticate is passed through to it.
telegram.maskingDomainWarning: Changing this invalidates every link already handed out — the domain is part of each client's secret.
telegram.publicHostHint: What goes into the links. Leave empty to use the panel's own public address.
telegram.publicPortHint: The port clients dial. Differs from the listen port when something sits in front.
telegram.preferIpHint: Which address family the proxy prefers when dialling Telegram.
telegram.outboundHint: Which outbound or endpoint the proxy reaches Telegram through. Direct uses this server's own address.
telegram.outboundNone: No outbounds or endpoints are configured yet — add one under Configuration to route Telegram through it.
telegram.outboundMissingWarning: The chosen exit no longer exists in the sing-box config. Telegram connections will fail until you pick another one or restore it.
telegram.socksPortHint: Loopback port carrying Telegram traffic to that exit. Change it only if something else on this host already uses it.
telegram.needsClient: Add a client first — the proxy has nothing to serve without one.
telegram.readOnly: The client file is read-only, so nothing here can be changed.

mieruPattern.title: Traffic pattern
mieruPattern.intro: Shapes mieru traffic against DPI. Client and server are configured independently — they do not have to match.
mieruPattern.unparsed: This value is not a valid mieru traffic pattern, so it is shown as-is. Clear it to use the editor.
mieruPattern.seedHint: The same seed gives the same generated pattern. Leave empty for a random one on every start.
mieruPattern.unlockAllHint: Lets generated values use the full range instead of the conservative subset.
mieruPattern.tcpFragmentHint: Splits some TCP packets into fragments. Adds latency; no effect on UDP.
mieruPattern.nonceHint: Random keeps the original nonce; Printable and Subset use ASCII characters; Fixed uses your own prefixes.
mieruPattern.customHexHint: Comma-separated hex strings without 0x, up to 12 bytes each; one is picked at random each time.
mieruPattern.applyToAllUdp: Apply to every UDP packet (otherwise only the first)
mieruPattern.paddingHint: Upper limits in bytes, 0-255. 0 disables that padding; empty lets mieru pick.
mieruPattern.lowEntropyHint: Data bits carried per 64-bit chunk; the rest is padding. Lower value = lower entropy but more traffic (mode 32 roughly doubles it).
